text.p: Ministers of the 18-member Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum said on Saturday they had made a "credible beginning" towards creating the world's biggest free trade zone.
In a joint statement at the end of a two-day meeting in Manila, the trade and foreign ministers also endorsed an expanded role for the private sector in APEC economies.
They also said they recognised the importance of boosting economic and technical cooperation among APEC members as a way to spread the booming region's wealth more equitably.
The statement, however, made no mention of any agreement on a joint APEC stance on information technology products at the World Trade Organisation meeting in Singapore next month.
The U.S. proposal, supported by Japan, has been one of the most divisive issues at the ministerial meeting, which is a prelude to a summit of APEC leaders in nearby Subic Bay on Monday.
